desk.headline: Recurring EBITDA up 35% to R$1.8bn and recurring profit up 80% to R$673m on distribution tariff reset; no financial guidance
results: Recurring EBITDA rose 35% to R$1.8bn and recurring net income rose 80% to R$673m; reported profit was R$688m, up 89%.
Distribution drove the quarter: its recurring EBITDA rose 70% to R$1.1bn after June's tariff reset (average 8.6% on the controllable part of the tariff) and 5.8% more billed volume.
Generation and transmission EBITDA fell about 4.5%, hit by wind curtailment.
Capex was R$991m, mostly in the grid and the Foz do Areia and Segredo hydro expansions; the sale of the Dona Francisca stake brought in R$151m.
Leverage was 2.7x net debt to EBITDA, and the average cost of debt fell 60 bp to 12.62% a year.

guidance.summary: Copel gives no revenue or profit guidance. Management said capex is on plan and the two big hydro expansions are on time and on budget.

points: The CEO credited the integrated model, with distribution gains offsetting weaker generation.
Management said its energy hedging worked well, much of 2027 exposure is covered and over half of 2029–30 energy is sold.
Copel will skip December's battery storage auction, saying expected returns are below its minimum.
September storms needed over 1,000 field crews and more than 3,700 replacement poles.
An investor day on 19 Nov will cover pumped-storage hydro and capital allocation.
